notes: SLA negotiation is central to closing — procurement will not sign without hard uptime number and acceptable credit schedule.
Customer preference: 99.99% uptime for production. Open to 99.95% with stronger credit tiers; wants examples/case studies.

Credit schedule under discussion (customer suggested): <99.99% = 5% monthly credit; <99.95% = 15% credit; <99.9% = 50% credit (capped). Redwood proposed alternative sliding scale tied to incident root cause.

Maintenance windows: Redwood proposal = monthly 2-hour window, 72h advance notice. Arkwind counter: allow maintenance only between 02:00-05:00 CET and never during month-end close (last 48h of month) or major earnings days.

Support response times asked by Arkwind: P1 (production down/high-sev) = 30 min initial response, P2 = 2 hours, P3 = 1 business day. They expect 24x7 via phone for P1 and dedicated technical account contact.
Reserved capacity ask: baseline 16 A100-eq GPUs (sustained), burst to +8 GPUs for traffic spikes. Want guaranteed throughput: 1500 tokens/s sustained at 256 seq for single-model route.
Throughput guarantees: request specific RPS/TPU-style guarantee per model family and degradation thresholds for fallback to cheaper model variants with automatic routing.
Data residency & audit: must see KMS integration, audit logging retention 3 years, SOC2 + ISO27001 required. Redwood asked about additional legal addendums for EU subsidiary.
Quote from Head of Infra: "We need predictable economics and a hard SLA — cost is secondary if the availability math is right."
Blocker detail: Arkwind legal wants explicit credit payout mechanism and maximum aggregate credits cap; mismatch on force majeure and scheduled maintenance exclusions.
POC plan: replay last 48 hours of production traffic into dedicated pool, run two 8-hour soak windows, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and error budget burn rate.
Operational ask: include a runbook that covers automated fallback to a lower-cost model variant, routing policy during GPU exhaustion, and a warm-warm failover region plan.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to annual reserved contract if SLA & maintenance constraints met; negotiating ARR band ~ $0.5M–$1.5M.
Next legal asks already queued: explicit maintenance blackout clause, SLA credit automation (applied to invoice), governing law for EU data should be Ireland.
AE notes: keep POC scoped small & measurable; prioritize proving 99.95% first, then negotiate premium for 99.99% once metrics stable.
SE notes: need to prepare a deterministic capacity model and define what constitutes an SLA incident (service-level error vs. customer misuse).
